surprises.description: PACCAR's Q4 gross-margin guide was 14%–15%, implying flattish sequential margins, rather than the expansion beyond 14.5% the preview said management had indicated. Management attributed the outlook to production-cost inefficiencies.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 guidance of 14% to 15% reflecting flattish sequential margins due to production cost inefficiencies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said on the Q2 call that Q4 margins expand beyond 14.5%”; “Buy-side wants 15.0%+.”

surprises.description: The 2027 US/Canada Class 8 forecast was a concrete 240,000–280,000 trucks, rather than a possible deferral of specifics to January amid regulatory uncertainty. The upper end is constructive, though the 240,000 lower end is flat with the top of the 2026 forecast range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PACCAR projects the 2027 US/Canada Class 8 market to grow to 240,000-280,000 trucks versus 240,000-260,000 in 2026, signaling a bullish outlook despite uncertainty on non-conformance penalty (NCP) levels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base = ‘we’ll give 2027 guidance in January.’” The preview also said management might hedge to “awaiting clarity.”

surprises.description: Q3 deliveries were 40,100, below PACCAR's roughly 42,000-unit company guide, even though they essentially matched the Street's 40,107 estimate. The call attributed the shortfall to supplier constraints.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 deliveries of 40,100 trucks came in below expectations due to supply chain constraints.”

surprises.description: The truck-segment result was $570 million, well above the preview's $317 million truck pretax estimate. That is a substantially stronger segment result than the preview's estimate, despite the weaker-than-expected Q4 margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Truck segment margin surged from $240 million in December 2025 to $570 million now.”

surprises.description: PACCAR Parts' margin declined slightly year over year, contrary to the preview's expectation that it would hold around 30%. The call also described fleets deferring maintenance purchases amid high operating costs and diesel prices, with CDL enforcement taking trucks out of service.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Parts margin declined slightly year-over-year due to mix shift”; elevated operating costs, high diesel prices, and trucks pulled out of service from CDL enforcement “led fleets to defer maintenance purchases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Parts holding ~30% margin at $1.79B is what keeps the 16x forward multiple defensible”; the preview also called for “~29.8% margin.”

surprises.description: Financial Services pretax income rose to $138 million, ahead of the preview's $132 million consensus estimate and its roughly $130 million base case. Stable finance margins and higher used-truck pricing supported the result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Financial Services pretax income rose 9.4% to $138 million on stable finance margins and higher used truck pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “PFS pretax | $132M”; the preview's base case assumed “PFS pretax | $130M.”

surprises.description: Customers were reported to prefer proven 200-milligram engines with an NCP over adopting unvetted lower-NOx technology, supporting demand for current platforms. That is a more reassuring demand signal amid the regulatory uncertainty the preview identified as a central debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers overwhelmingly prefer buying proven 200-milligram engines with an NCP for 2027 rather than adopting unvetted lower-NOx engine technology, keeping demand strong for current platforms.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “the pre-buy question” and said that if management hedged to “awaiting clarity,” it would validate the derating.

surprises.description: PACCAR generated $2.5 billion of operating cash over nine months, exceeding net income. The preview did not identify cash conversion as a key issue, so this was an additional positive reported metric rather than a result against a stated forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PACCAR generated $2.5 billion in cash from operations over nine months, exceeding net income.”
